title: Interfaces
hook: An interface is a CLR contract a class or struct can implement many of. Default interface methods let you evolve that contract. Explicit implementation hides a member until you cast.

sections.heading: Contracts, not types with fields
sections.prose: Interfaces declare members without instance fields. Classes, structs, and records implement them. A struct implementing an interface boxes when you store it as the interface type — relevant for cache-key structs. Interfaces are how a worker depends on IBus without taking a RabbitMQ type. That is composition with a type-checked seam (previous composition topic).

sections.heading: Default interface methods and explicit implementation
sections.prose: Default interface methods (C# 8) put a body on the interface. Existing implementers compile against the new member without source changes; they can still override it. Diamond inheritance of defaults is resolved with explicit reimplementation rules — interviews like this. Explicit implementation (IBus.Publish) keeps the method off the class’s public surface so a type can implement two interfaces with the same member name without polluting IntelliSense.

snippets.label: DIM plus explicit implementation
snippets.explanation: PublishAsync without a token is a default interface method. The core method is explicit: you must use the IBus view. The class surface stays a sealed worker collaborator.

sections.heading: Versioning
sections.prose: Adding a non-default method to a public interface is a breaking change. DIM is the evolution hatch, with the caveat that implementers who never recompile still get your default, for better or worse. Prefer small interfaces (ISP) over kitchen-sink IWorkerBase.

interviewTakeaways: DIM evolves contracts; explicit implementation disambiguates and hides.
commonPitfalls: Fat interfaces that force fake implementations.
Forgetting a default method is only visible through the interface type unless redeclared on the class.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS interfaces are structural and erased. A matching object literal satisfies them. C# interfaces are nominal and require an implements (or a generated wrapper).
JS will call obj.publish() if it exists. C# will not compile a call without a type that has the member; interface casts fail at runtime if the object is the wrong CLR type.
